description: Reads an image file as a source of voltages: give it a position and it puts out the colour of the pixel at that point

params.text: Formats the three colour outputs as red, green and blue in one setting and as hue, saturation and value in the other
Sets what voltage range the colour outputs cover: -5V to +5V in one position, 0V to 10V in the other
Sets what voltage range the position jacks cover: -5V to +5V in one position, 0V to 10V in the other
Held down, opens a file dialogue for choosing the image; PNG, JPEG, BMP, GIF, PSD, HDR, PIC and PNM files are offered

inputs.text: Channel 1 is the horizontal position to read from and channel 2 the vertical; patching this leaves the separate X and Y jacks unread
The horizontal position to read from; it is unread while the two-channel position jack has a cable in it
The vertical position to read from; it is unread while the two-channel position jack has a cable in it

outputs.text: Channels 1, 2 and 3 carry the three colour components of the pixel at the given point
The red or hue of the pixel at the given point, depending on the colour-format switch
The green or saturation of the pixel at the given point, depending on the colour-format switch
The blue or value of the pixel at the given point, depending on the colour-format switch

notes: nothing comes out of any output until an image has been loaded with the load button
a position past the edge of the picture is folded back into range rather than clamped, so a sweep wider than the picture reads it mirrored
the picture is shown on the panel at whatever size it was loaded at, and clicking the picture does nothing

inputs.1:
±5V · continuous · one channel only

unpatched it reads 0V.
inputs.2:

unpatched it reads 0V.
